papers.title: HydraInfer: Hybrid Disaggregated Scheduling for Multimodal Large Language Model Serving
papers.system_note: Hybrid Encode-Prefill-Decode disaggregation for MLLM serving. Schedules encode/prefill/decode onto separate heterogeneous inference instances, flexibly reallocates resources across stages, and uses stage-level batching/load balancing with visual-language parallelism. arXiv v2 reports up to 4x throughput over vLLM on an 8xH800 node while meeting the 90th-percentile request SLO. Adjacent multimodal SYS trunk; transferable to composite Physical-AI pipelines, not a robot-specific runtime.

papers.title: JoyNexus: Service-Oriented Multi-Tenant Post-Training for VLA Models
papers.system_note: multi-tenant VLA service substrate spanning SFT, RL, rollout and evaluation; Master Service controls resource allocation/session placement/service routing; resident Training/Inference/Environment Services preserve tenant-private action modules, optimizer/policy-version state, use separate global Training and Inference queues, group batching across compatible VLA schemas, service-level fault isolation and elastic rollout scaling. Direct Physical-AI service/runtime infrastructure rather than an algorithmic VLA accelerator.

papers.title: Enabling Disaggregated Multi-Stage MLLM Inference via GPU-Internal Scheduling and Resource Sharing
papers.system_note: end-to-end MLLM serving stack: FlashCodec collaboratively uses multi-GPU/NVDEC resources for low-latency video decoding; UnifiedServe logically decouples preprocessing, encode/prefill and decode while physically sharing GPU resources, uses asynchronous coordinated workers and intermediate-state buffering to reduce inter-stage blocking/resource fragmentation. Reports up to 3.0x more served requests, 1.5x tighter SLOs, and up to 4.4x throughput versus baselines. Adjacent multimodal SYS trunk with direct relevance to composite Physical-AI pipelines.

Important infrastructure omission recovered from JoyNexus/RL-VLA3 same-group census. Current paper explicitly describes an early construction stage (single task on Isaac Sim 5.1), so maturity is rated A- rather than A/A+. No official public implementation repository was verified in this run.

papers.title: D-VLA: A High-Concurrency Distributed Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.system_note: Distributed embodied/VLA RL systems framework. Plane Decoupling separates high-frequency training data from low-frequency weight-control traffic; a four-thread Swimlane pipeline overlaps sampling, inference, gradient computation and parameter distribution; dual-pool VRAM management and topology-aware replication address simulator/model resource conflict, memory fragmentation and communication. Included as Physical-AI training/rollout infrastructure rather than an algorithmic VLA accelerator.

papers.title: RL-VLA3: A Flexible and Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for VLA Training
papers.venue: arXiv v2; earlier version published at ICLR 2026 SPOT Workshop
papers.system_note: Fully asynchronous distributed VLA RL infrastructure. The current arXiv v2 uses fine-grained asynchronous interaction across simulation, inference and training, with dynamic batching schedulers and flexible environment sharding; it reports up to 85.2% throughput improvement over synchronous baselines while preserving sample efficiency and validates scaling from 8 to 256 GPUs. This is a direct systems predecessor/neighbor of D-VLA and belongs in the Physical-AI training/rollout infrastructure trunk, not ordinary Efficient-VLA algorithms. An older ICLR 2026 SPOT Workshop version reports different throughput figures; keep evidence source/version scoped rather than mixing them. No official implementation repository was verified in this run.

SOP: A Scalable Online Post-Training System for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.system_note: Fleet-scale online post-training infrastructure for generalist VLA deployment. Multiple robots stream on-policy trajectories and human interventions to a centralized cloud learner and asynchronously receive updated policies, forming a low-latency actor-learner loop that is algorithm-agnostic (demonstrated with HG-DAgger and RECAP). AGIBOT reports 4-robot post-training reaching 92.5% success within 3h versus 80.5% for one robot and reaching 80% success in 71.7 min versus 173.6 min (2.4x faster); updated parameters are synchronized back to the fleet within minutes. Included as CORE_SYS because its primary contribution is a distributed fleet/cloud execution-learning substrate rather than a VLA algorithm itself. No official implementation repository was verified in this run.

papers.title: Learning while Deploying: Fleet-Scale Reinforcement Learning for Generalist Robot Policies
papers.system_note: Follow-on fleet deployment-to-learning loop from the AGIBOT Finch/Jianlan Luo lineage. A fleet of 16 dual-arm robots uploads heterogeneous deployment experience into shared replay and receives periodically improved shared policies; the paper reaches 95% average success across eight real-world tasks, including 3-5 minute long-horizon tasks. Kept at SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY because the paper's central novelty is offline-to-online RL (DIVL + QAM) even though it has real fleet-scale infrastructure and continual deployment semantics. No official implementation repository was verified in this run.

papers.title: RLinf-VLA: A Unified and Efficient Framework for Reinforcement Learning of Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.system_note: Unified scalable VLA+RL systems framework. It standardizes diverse VLA architectures, RL algorithms and heterogeneous simulators behind one interface, and exposes collocated, disaggregated and hybrid GPU resource-allocation modes across rendering, inference and training. The hybrid fine-grained pipeline allocation reports 1.61x-1.88x speedup within the system study and the project reports up to 2.27x versus existing framework baselines. Official RLinf documentation lists the work as RSS 2026; the shared RLinf repository has roughly 3.6k stars in the current public crawl. Included as CORE_SYS because the primary contribution is unified resource allocation/execution infrastructure for embodied RL rather than a VLA algorithm.

papers.title: RLinf-USER: A Unified and Extensible System for Real-World Online Policy Learning in Embodied AI
papers.system_note: Real-world online-policy-learning system that treats physical robots as first-class schedulable hardware resources alongside GPUs. USER provides automatic heterogeneous-robot discovery/management/scheduling, adaptive cloud-edge tunneling and distributed data channels, SM-aware weight synchronization, a fully asynchronous data-generation/training/sync pipeline, and a persistent cache-aware buffer with crash recovery and historical-data reuse. Official RLinf documentation lists the work as RSS 2026. The system-efficiency study reports asynchronous pi0+HG-DAgger generation/training periods improved by 1.20x/5.70x and CNN+SAC by 1.55x/4.61x versus synchronous execution. Included as CORE_SYS because it is a direct Physical-AI resource/runtime substrate spanning robots, GPUs, networking and persistent state.

StreamMind separates latency-critical real-time interaction and proactive monitoring into independently scheduled frontend workers while backend workers asynchronously construct persistent multimodal memory, perform historical recall and external search. The design makes persistent state reuse and frontend/backend decoupling first-class runtime mechanisms for hour-scale streaming agents.
papers.key_results: StreamArena contains 243 full-length videos averaging 88.8 minutes and 3,646 timestamped open-ended tasks across real-time perception, historical retrospection, tool use and proactive interaction. The official project reports StreamMind weighted query-to-answer latency of 27.5 s versus 81.4 s for the same offline backbone (66.2% reduction), with the system leading evaluated streaming baselines across all four capabilities.
papers.maturity_note: Strong streaming-runtime plus evaluation-infrastructure contribution with official code/data, but the full StreamMind agent implementation is not yet released; CORE_SYS/A rather than A+.

papers.title: Joint Age-of-Latent and Resource Minimization for Wireless Multi-Camera Perception With Temporal Window Selection
papers.open_source: No official implementation repository verified in this run.
papers.system_contribution: Freshness-aware edge/resource-control formulation for wireless multi-camera Physical-AI perception. Age-of-Latent (AoL) tracks task-relevant latent freshness at the base station; task-level temporal-window selection is jointly coupled with slot-level encoder selection, camera scheduling and NOMA power allocation under prediction-reliability constraints.
papers.key_results: On a warehouse multi-camera RF dataset, CoLA reports the best AoL-resource tradeoff among evaluated benchmarks while preserving prediction reliability, with larger gains under prolonged and severe camera outages. The evidence is numerical/simulation-based; no deployed serving/runtime implementation is claimed.
papers.maturity_note: System-facing edge/freshness/resource-management work, but the primary contribution is algorithmic optimization and simulation rather than a reusable serving runtime or resource manager; therefore SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY/A, Routes 4/5/8.

papers.title: TypeGo: An OS Runtime for Embodied Agents
papers.system_note: OS-style runtime for embodied agents. TypeGo turns concurrent embodied tasks into processes/PCBs, uses a Skill Kernel to arbitrate typed physical subsystems, preempts/resumes tasks with source-dependent semantics, runs S0-S3 asynchronous planning loops at multiple timescales, and overlaps speculative skill streaming with physical execution. Unitree Go2 prototype reports 50% lower per-step delay than step-by-step planning and 73% lower time-to-first-action than monolithic planning, with ~200 ms S3 scheduling and ~50 ms reflex overhead.

papers.title: TimelyLLM: Time-sensitive LLM Serving System for Physical-I/O Limited Agents
papers.venue: ACM MobiSys 2026 — Best Paper Runner-up / Best Artifact Runner-up
papers.open_source: Award page verifies Best Artifact Runner-up; no canonical public implementation repository was verified in this run.
papers.system_contribution: Time-sensitive serving for multiple robotic agents. TimelyLLM segments plan generation around physical-I/O execution opportunities and schedules LLM work according to segment timing needs, explicitly exploiting overlap between robot execution and future-plan generation instead of FCFS batching.
papers.key_results: The paper reports up to 1.97x higher time utility and 84% lower overall waiting time across robotic applications. MobiSys 2026 officially lists the work as Best Paper Runner-up and Best Artifact Runner-up.
papers.maturity_note: Direct Physical-AI serving/scheduling system with formal MobiSys 2026 recognition; historical omission recovered during TypeGo/TypeFly/TimelyLLM lineage census.

papers.title: TypeFly: Low-Latency Drone Planning With Large Language Models
papers.open_source: Official Apache-2.0 repository verified; public crawl showed 110 stars / 25 forks during this run.
papers.system_contribution: Edge/cloud robot-planning runtime built around MiniSpec, a token-efficient control language with stream interpretation so a drone can begin executing before the full LLM plan completes; local vision service and robot skill runtime reduce response latency and keep image processing off the cloud path.
papers.key_results: The TMC paper reports substantially lower response time than prior approaches; the arXiv/project description reports up to 62% response-time reduction from MiniSpec plus stream interpretation. Because the primary novelty mixes compact plan representation with runtime execution, it remains SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY rather than CORE_SYS.
papers.maturity_note: Published IEEE TMC 2025 with official public repo and project page; important predecessor to TimelyLLM/TypeGo but not primarily a general serving/resource-management substrate.

papers.title: JoyAI-VL-Interaction: Real-Time Vision-Language Interaction Intelligence
papers.open_source: Official Apache-2.0 repo verified; public GitHub crawl showed about 1.8k stars / 182 forks on 2026-09-03. Model, data, training recipe, deployable system, vLLM deployment and LiveKit branch are public.
papers.system_contribution: Always-on visual interaction stack around an 8B interaction model. The deployable system streams continuous video, keeps long-horizon state, exposes pluggable ASR/TTS/memory/UI, and splits execution into a real-time user loop plus an asynchronous background-model/agent delegation loop; five services run on standard vLLM infrastructure.
papers.key_results: The paper reports hours of continuous video with sub-second latency and human preference wins of 77.6% vs Doubao and 87.9% vs Gemini across six live scenarios. These results primarily validate interaction quality/timing rather than serving throughput/resource efficiency.
papers.maturity_note: High-value real-time multimodal/Physical-AI boundary system and unusually complete open deployment stack, but the main novelty is the interaction model/training paradigm rather than a new scheduler, resource manager or cache allocator; therefore SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY/A+, Routes 3/5/7/11 rather than CORE_SYS.

papers.title: A Composable Evaluation System for Reproducible Omni-Modal Foundation Model Evaluation
papers.open_source: Official Apache-2.0 repository verified; GitHub API reported 16 stars / 2 forks at 2026-09-03 11:00 CST. Public code includes the evaluator, dashboard, demos, tests and server entrypoints.
papers.system_contribution: Composable omni-modal evaluation infrastructure. A unified intermediate schema decouples inference engines from evaluation frameworks (N+M adapters instead of N×M pairwise integrations), with HuggingFace/vLLM/SGLang/API backends, multiple evaluator frameworks, provenance-rich run artifacts, a shared dashboard, and federated many-to-many inference-server/evaluation-client execution that pools fragmented GPU capacity and leverages serving-engine continuous batching.
papers.key_results: The paper exposes four inference backends, four evaluation frameworks and 1000+ benchmarks in the paper (the current repo advertises 2,820 benchmark tasks). Under the same GPU allocation, federated evaluation reports 1.3×–2.8× wall-time speedup over per-process evaluation. The built-in CPU-capable verifier reduces cross-engine/prompt score variance relative to rule-based scoring. OmniEvaluator was used during HyperCLOVA X 8B Omni development.
papers.maturity_note: CORE_SYS/A+ because the main contribution is reusable evaluation/serving infrastructure, not a model algorithm. Route 9 is primary; Route 11 is secondary because it directly composes omni-modal serving backends and shares inference servers. Fresh project with modest adoption so far; upstream evaluator bugs can still propagate and the verifier only judges textual correctness.
